correctness.rationale: Exact rank-two orthogonal decomposition proves the chi-square error factorization. Standard angular integrals (with positive denominators) produce E[r^2]; the three-query baseline variance is direct from independent Gaussian quadratic forms. The palindromic quartic becomes an increasing quadratic in t+t^{-1} for t>=1, giving one threshold. A dominated-convergence argument proves persistence under full-rank perturbations. The packaged verifier passed 545 supporting checks; sampling was not substituted for the proof. Scope is all finite n>=2, rank-two PSD A with a>=b>0.

value.rationale: At the smallest three-matrix-vector-product allocation of commonly used Gaussian trace estimators, the exact spectral threshold identifies when the low-rank variance reduction phase is worth its two products. Both sides occur naturally: isotropic rank two favors direct probing while sufficiently spiked rank two favors Hutch++. The contrast persists for nearby full-rank matrices. The result is an interpretable, motivated method-comparison benchmark; it does not purport to improve all algorithms or establish query optimality, and its known low-rank rank-identification alternatives are stated as limits.
